title: JPA Relationship Loading
summary: Understand lazy and eager loading before choosing a fetch plan.

richText: Fetch timing controls when related entity data is loaded.
LAZY requests deferred loading. The provider may load the relationship when application code accesses it.
EAGER requires the relationship to be loaded. It does not guarantee that all data arrives in one SQL query.
JPA defaults one-to-many and many-to-many relationships to LAZY. Many-to-one and one-to-one default to EAGER.
Choose the data needed by the current operation. An eager relationship can load data that operation never uses.
A persistence context tracks managed entities during persistence work.

A deferred relationship may need an active persistence context to load its data. With Hibernate, accessing an uninitialized relationship after the context closes can throw LazyInitializationException.
Read required data inside the service transaction. Return a response object containing the needed values instead of relying on later loading during JSON serialization.
The N+1 query problem occurs when one query loads N parent rows and accessing their relationships triggers additional queries for those rows.
Inspect the SQL for the operation. Changing every relationship to EAGER does not guarantee the problem is solved.
A JPQL fetch join loads the selected relationship as part of the query. An entity graph is another way to specify which relationships the operation needs.
Fetching a collection can duplicate parent rows in SQL results. Collection fetch joins also require care when paginating.

It returns all posts. Add a bounded query when the application needs only part of the table.
